mappings.text: a. Define and document the types of accounts allowed and specifically prohibited for use within the system; b. Assign account managers; c. Access authorizations (i.e., privileges) and [Assignment: organization-defined attributes (as required)] for each account; e. Require approvals by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] for requests to create accounts; f. Create, enable, modify, disable, and remove accounts in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined policy, procedures, prerequisites, and criteria]; g. Monitor the use of accounts; h. [Assignment: organization-defined time period] when system usage or need-to-know changes for an individual; i. Authorize access to the system based on: 1. A valid access authorization; 2. mappings.title: Access Enforcement
mappings.text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Access enforcement is the technical gate that makes allocated privileges binding; 01.c is only real where approved authorizations are enforced.

mappings.title: Least Privilege
mappings.text: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.

mappings.title: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
mappings.text: a. Determine and document the [Assignment: organization-defined authority] that permits the [Assignment: organization-defined processing] of personally identifiable information; and b. Restrict the [Assignment: organization-defined processing] of personally identifiable information to only that which is authorized.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Restricting processing of PII to what is legally authorized is the statutory-basis core of 06.d.
mappings.technical_validation_method: PII regex/entropy sweep flags personal data discovered in locations or systems with no declared processing authority in the scan profile.

hitrust_control.control_title: Data Protection and Privacy of Covered Information

mappings.title: Information Management and Retention
mappings.text: Manage and retain information within the system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines and operational requirements.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Managing and retaining information per applicable law is 06.d's retention/limitation obligation in 800-53 terms.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Traverser inventories covered-information files with last-modified ages against declared retention windows; over-retention flagged in the findings aggregator.

mappings.title: Protection of Information at Rest
mappings.text: Protect the [Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity] of the following information at rest: [Assignment: organization-defined information at rest].
mappings.mapping_rationale: Protection of information at rest is the technical safeguard 06.d expects for stored covered information; entropy/chi-square analysis verifies at-rest protection empirically.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Multi-attribute cryptographic pipeline: regex detection of PII/PHI/PAN patterns in traversed files combined with Shannon-entropy and chi-square tests to distinguish encrypted from plaintext storage; flag covered information found unencrypted or outside sanctioned locations.

mappings.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
mappings.text: a. Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the system and hosted applications [Assignment: organization-defined frequency and/or randomly in accordance with organization-defined process] and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the system are identified and reported; b. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools and techniques that facilitate interoperability among tools and automate parts of the vulnerability management process by using standards for: 1. Enumerating platforms, software flaws, and improper configurations; 2. Formatting checklists and test procedures; and 3. Measuring vulnerability impact; c. Analyze vulnerability scan reports and results from vulnerability monitoring; d. Remediate legitimate vulnerabilities [Assignment: organization-defined response times] in accordance with an organizational assessment of risk; e. Share information obtained from the vulnerability monitoring process and control assessments with [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] to help eliminate similar vulnerabilities in other systems; and f. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools that include the capability to readily update the vulnerabilities to be scanned.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Vulnerability monitoring and scanning is the direct 800-53 implementation of 10.m: obtain vulnerability information, scan, evaluate exposure.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Regex audit of service configuration files (SSH/TLS/web server) for weak ciphers, legacy protocol versions, and insecure directives; extraction of software version strings from package manifests and binaries for comparison against known-vulnerable version ranges.

mappings.title: Flaw Remediation
mappings.text: a. Identify, report, and correct system flaws; b. Test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation; c. Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of the release of the updates; and d. Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Flaw remediation is the 'take appropriate measures' step of 10.m: identify, report, correct, and patch within defined periods.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Version-string extraction from package manifests/binaries compared against known-vulnerable ranges; finding age across scan ledgers evidences remediation timeliness.

mappings.title: Media Access

mappings.mapping_rationale: Restricting media access to defined roles is the access-control face of 09.q information handling.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Recursive file-system traverser and ZIP archive chunker locate covered information across storage paths, including temp, recycle, and archive locations; entropy analysis detects residual plaintext sensitive data on paths staged for re-use or disposal.

mappings.title: Media Sanitization
mappings.text: a. Sanitize [Assignment: organization-defined system media] prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse using [Assignment: organization-defined sanitization techniques and procedures]; and b. Employ sanitization mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Media sanitization before disposal, release, or re-use is 09.q's disposal/re-use element; residual-data detection is its software verification.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Entropy analysis and covered-information regex over re-use/disposal-staged paths detect recoverable plaintext that sanitization should have removed.

mappings.title: Event Logging
mappings.text: a. Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function: [Assignment: organization-defined event types that the system is capable of logging]; b. Coordinate the event logging function with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information to guide and inform the selection criteria for events to be logged; c. Specify the following event types for logging within the system: [Assignment: organization-defined event types (subset of the event types defined in AU-02a.) along with the frequency of (or situation requiring) logging for each identified event type]; d. Provide a rationale for why the event types selected for logging are deemed to be adequate to support after-the-fact investigations of incidents; and e. Review and update the event types selected for logging [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
mappings.mapping_rationale: Event logging - selecting and enabling the event types systems log - is the foundation 09.aa's 'audit logs are produced' clause rests on.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Audit Ledger Synthesis: every scan produces a tamper-evident kintsugi_scan.json evidence ledger; the scanner additionally verifies presence, permissions (via UID/GID module), and non-zero recency of host audit/syslog artifacts and logging daemon configuration files.

mappings.title: Content of Audit Records
mappings.text: Ensure that audit records contain information that establishes the following: a. What type of event occurred; b. When the event occurred; c. Where the event occurred; d. Source of the event; e. Outcome of the event; and f. Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Content of audit records supplies 09.aa's what/when/where/source/outcome/identity record requirements.
mappings.technical_validation_method: Sampling parser over discovered logs verifies record fields; logging-daemon configuration regex confirms field capture is enabled.

mappings.title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
mappings.text: a. Review and analyze system audit records [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] for indications of [Assignment: organization-defined inappropriate or unusual activity] and the potential impact of the inappropriate or unusual activity; b. Report findings to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]; and c. Adjust the level of audit record review, analysis, and reporting within the system when there is a change in risk based on law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources of information.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Review, analysis, and reporting of audit records is the 'assist future investigations and monitoring' purpose clause of 09.aa.
mappings.technical_validation_method: kintsugi_scan.json ledger provides reviewable, timestamped findings; staleness checks on host logs evidence whether review-ready records exist.

mappings.title: Protection of Audit Information
mappings.text: a. Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion; and b. Alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information.
mappings.mapping_rationale: Protection of audit information from unauthorized access/modification/deletion is 09.aa's retention-custody requirement.
mappings.technical_validation_method: UID/GID and permission-bit audit of log files/directories; hash comparison of ledger files across runs surfaces tampering.
